doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Hippies, parents and the American Music Awards
summary: His theory of why youth rejected jazz, and complaints about mediocrity.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I have a philosophy on that too. A reason why, the whyness or why of that. It’s during the groupie period in this country, when the groupies and people all decided, hey, they’re going to cop out and just become whatever. You know, during Woodstock, what do you call it.
Hippies, okay. See hippies was — hip.

But the reason for that, I mean what I’m getting at, and this is a funny philosophy but when these people start turning off, the first things they turn off was their parents. Old fashioned, old hat. So in turning their parents off they turned off everything the parents dug, everything they liked, jazz was one of them. Jazz was one of the things, hey I don’t like it because my parents like it, so hey, I’m going to go over here and hear this other shit. You want to bleep that off or keep that in. But anyway, so that’s where the division began. They didn’t like it because their parents liked it. And from there it just got bigger and bigger and bigger and bigger and bigger, in the meantime this other thing was thrust, thrust, thrust, thrust, next thing you know, they had a program on television last week, I guess it was sometime last week, called “American Music” or something, where they gave out awards.
Oh yeah, the American Music Awards.
Man that was some of the —

Hey man I’m not bitter, I’m not envious, I’m not jealous, hey man it’s straight ahead for everybody. I mean the more the better. But man I didn’t believe some of that stuff. I did not believe what these people considered talent. I did not believe what these people © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

considered good. Mediocrity is king now man. You know? And unfortunately man, young people don’t have an opportunity to decide what is good and what is bad and what is different. They don’t even have a culture. They have not — I mean at least we developed a culture so that we could look back and say hey well so-and-so did so-and-so and so-and-so is responsible for this. Hey well man, that’s a dynamite chair. Wow, it was designed, and we have this. What they have is — how outlandish can you be? How funky can you be? Shit. Don’t let me get started man. I’m not bitter man. It’s cool, man.
